CODE
Art. 2.3.81. 
Optional judicial correction in equity 
Without prejudice to paragraph 2, the Family Court may, where the marriage is dissolved by divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown between the spouses, grant to the aggrieved spouse, at his request, compensation to be paid by the other spouse, provided that circumstances have unfavorably and unforeseeably changed since the conclusion of the matrimonial agreement of separation as to property or since the date of the application for separation as to property, so that the regime chosen would result, to the detriment of the applicant spouse, in manifestly unfair consequences, having regard to the property situation of both spouses.
The compensation to be awarded remedies these manifestly unfair consequences and may not exceed one-third of the net value of the spouses' joint acquests at the time of the dissolution of the marriage, from which must then be deducted the net value of the claimant spouse's personal acquisitions. The acquisitions of the spouses within the meaning of this paragraph are determined in accordance with articles 2.3.65 to 2.3.69.
The claim for compensation is examined as part of the procedure for the liquidation of the matrimonial property regime.
The spouses who opt for the regime of separation as to property record in their matrimonial agreement their agreement as to whether or not to include this right to compensation, with or without derogatory terms.
The notary draws the spouses' attention to the obligation set out in paragraph 1 and to the legal consequences arising from their choice of whether or not to include the right to compensation, with or without derogating terms and conditions. Under penalty of liability, the notary shall expressly mention the spouses' choice in the matrimonial agreement.
